subject: Midpoint OKR alignment: scope adjustments, resource swaps & QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midpoint OKR alignment: scope adjustments, resource swaps & QBR artifacts

Team —

Attaching a short snapshot of current OKR progress and a draft QBR deck (see attachments). I scrolled through the numbers and there are three pockets where we need quick decisions to stay on track for the quarter:

1) Inference latency SLAs (Objective: 99th %ile <= 220ms) — the runtime team is currently tracking ~240ms for several long-tail customers (ACME included).

2) Throughput / capacity for Dedicated customers (Objective: predictable 300k requests/day) — burst capacity plan requires an additional 0.5 GPU-equivalent from the shared pool to meet scheduled ramp.

3) Internal reliability experiments (Objective: deploy KV-cache customization) — experiment needs one infra engineer for 4 weeks to unblock QC.

Asks:
- Vivek: can you propose a concrete resource swap (which tickets/owners we deprioritize) and the SLA fallback plan? I need a recommendation by EOD tomorrow.
- Laura: can you surface any customer escalations that would force us to prioritize ACME vs others? If ACME is blocking QBR narrative, flag what we must deliver in the next 10 business days.
- Tessa: please update the QBR slide (linked) with the top-3 risk bullets and a one-line mitigation per risk.

Attachments: OKR_snapshot_Jul2026.pdf (summary, 2 pages), QBR_slide_draft_v1.pptx (5 slides), dependency_risks.xlsx (living tracker).

I put the ACME account at the top of the notes because their ramp is live and they requested a readiness confirmation for their upcoming launch. If we re-scope anything, we should document the trade-offs in the deck.

Thanks — short sync later this afternoon if needed.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
Camila.Reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint OKR alignment: scope adjustments, resource swaps & QBR artifacts

Thanks Camila — read and agree with the ask. Quick proposal: 

1) Latency: move forward with a short-term patch (kernel-level tweak + tighter batching controls) that reduces 99p by ~12–15ms for impacted models. Impact: requires 0.25 FTE of serving-engine hours over two sprints.

2) Dedicated capacity burst: reassign one half of the experimental GPU budget (0.5 GPU-equivalent) from the reliability experiment to the Dedicated burst pool for 6 weeks. That shift gives us breathing room for ACME's ramp.

3) Reliability experiment: pause the KV-cache customization full rollout; keep a proof-of-concept branch running but remove the weekly experiment support until the Dedicated burst window closes.

Stake trade-offs (short): we push out the reliability full rollout by ~3 weeks, which increases probability of a regression not being caught in non-production.

Owner/next steps:
- I will open an owner-change RFC for the resource swap (infra-ticket #INF-4892) and tag the infra leads.
- Laura, if ACME must be prioritized higher, we should short-circuit the swap and identify a different deprioritization candidate (e.g., deprioritize the new dev UX polish for now).

Attaching a rough capacity table to show the impact — see dependency_risks.xlsx.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Agree with Vivek's plan in principle. A few customer notes from CS:
- Maria Lopez at AcmeCorp called this morning and emphasized that their GA date is now firm (2026-08-18). They will not accept a degraded SLA at launch.
- ProdOps (external) also indicated they will run a full-headroom test July 30 — if we don't provide dedicated burst capacity we risk failing their test and triggering an escalation.

If we commit to the burst: we must prepare a short rollback/fallback playbook for ACME in case the burst induces instability. I recommend one page with: who to call, failover model variant, and auto-throttle thresholds.

Quick asks from my side:
- Vivek: include the emergency rollback steps in the RFC (INF-4892).
- Camila: add the ACME headroom test and its date to the QBR slide and the risks table.
- Tessa: add the one-line mitigation 'prepare rollback playbook' to slide 3.

I can draft the one-page rollback playbook with ProdOps if you want — I have a 30-min slot tomorrow morning at 10:00.

— Laura

Thanks — good alignment. Summary / decisions: 

1) Approve Vivek's swap: move 0.5 GPU-equivalent from experiments to Dedicated burst (6-week window). Vivek will open RFC INF-4892 and include emergency rollback steps. Owner: Vivek — RFC by tomorrow EOD.

2) Pause the KV-cache rollout to preserve experiment bandwidth; maintain POC branch. Owner: Vivek / Experiments lead.

3) Customer items: Laura to draft one-page rollback playbook and coordinate with ProdOps. Camila to confirm ACME's July 30 headroom test in writing (Maria, can you confirm in-thread?)

4) QBR deck: Tessa to update slides with risks, mitigation one-liners, and the ACME headroom test date. Updated deck link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/QBR-ACME-2026 (please update slide deck by EOD tomorrow).

Actions & deadlines:
- Vivek: RFC INF-4892 + rollback steps — due 2026-07-23 EOD (owner: Vivek).
- Laura: Draft rollback playbook and meet with ProdOps — meeting tomorrow 10:00am.
- Tessa: Slide updates + attach dependency_risks.xlsx — due 2026-07-23 EOD.
- Camila: Follow-up confirmation from Maria and include confirmation in final QBR notes.

Maria — can you confirm the July 30 headroom test and whether ACME requires any special test vectors or traffic shapes?

Thanks all — I think this keeps our OKRs intact while making a pragmatic trade for the QBR narrative.

Attachments: QBR_slide_draft_v1.pptx (updated), OKR_snapshot_Jul2026.pdf

— Camila
